government_id.description: Signer's CPF (11 digits) or CNPJ (14 characters; may be alphanumeric). Formatting is accepted and the value is normalized on save. Required before the signer can use a verification method that identifies them by CPF.

role_id.description: The template role ID associated with the signer.

id.description: An existing signer's ID. Send either `id` or `email`; `id` wins when both are sent, and an unknown `id` returns `400`.

email.description: Used when `id` is not sent: the account's signer with this email is reused, or a new one is created with `name`.

name.description: Full name for a signer created from `email`.

whatsapp_phone_number.description: WhatsApp number for a signer created from `email`.

verification_method.description: Verification method for this signer. If provided without notification_methods, the notification method is inferred. Defaults to Email. `DigitalCertificate` has the signer sign with their own ICP-Brasil certificate — it requires the Digital Certificate feature, the signer must have a CPF or CNPJ in `government_id` (a CPF requires that person's certificate; a CNPJ requires an e-CNPJ for that company), must be alone in its signing step, and is charged 0.5 credits per signer. It is refused with `400` when the template has placed signer fields, because certificate signers sign only virtual assignments. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires the ID Document + Face Match feature, the signer must have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee. Only applies to signers (not copy receivers).

notification_methods.description: Notification method codes for this signer. If provided without verification_method, the verification method is inferred. Defaults to Email. Only one method allowed per signer.

step.description: Positive integer that controls signing order. Signers sharing the same step sign in parallel; a step activates only after every signer in the previous step has signed. If supplied for any role it must be supplied for all, forming a contiguous sequence starting at 1. Copy receivers ignore this field.

editor_fields.description: Values for the fields placed on the template's `Editor` role, baked into the generated document. The `Editor` role takes no `signers` entry: it is filled only through this list. Every field placed on it needs an entry with a non-empty `value` (`400` otherwise); when it has no fields, send nothing. In `signers`, every `Signer` role needs an entry (`400` otherwise), and a `CopyReceiver` role takes an entry only for someone who should receive the certified document; a copy receiver's `verification_method`, `notification_methods` and `step` are ignored.

field_id.description: The field identifier, matching the field_id in the template data.

value.description: The value to assign to the field.

name.description: Title for the document. Defaults to the template name.

expires_at.description: Assignment expiration date (ISO 8601). No expiration by default. Must be at least one hour in the future. A UTC offset in the value is honored (`2026-12-31T23:59:59-03:00` is `2027-01-01T02:59:59Z`); a value without one is read as UTC, and a date alone (`2026-12-31`) means 23:59 UTC that day.

tags.description: Tag names to attach to the new document. Names that don't exist are auto-created. The template's default-document-tags are always applied; values here are merged on top (duplicates removed).

method.description: `virtual` signs without input fields; `collect` places input fields on pages. Signers with `DigitalCertificate` verification need `virtual` (`collect` returns `400`).

verification_method.description: How the signer's identity is verified before signing. `Email` (default) sends a one-time code to the signer's email; `Whatsapp` sends the code over WhatsApp — the verification itself is not billed, but it requires the WhatsApp notification channel, so the signer costs 0.45 credits (available only on paid subscriptions); `DigitalCertificate` has the signer sign with their own ICP-Brasil certificate (A1/A3) — it requires the Digital Certificate feature, the signer must have a CPF or CNPJ in `government_id`, must be alone in its signing step, needs `method: virtual` (a `collect` assignment with a `DigitalCertificate` signer returns `400`), and is charged 0.5 credits per signer. A CPF requires that person's certificate (an e-CPF, or an e-CNPJ naming them as legal representative); a CNPJ requires an e-CNPJ for that company, from any of its representatives. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires the ID Document + Face Match feature, the signer must have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee. Omit to default to `Email`.

notification_methods.description: How the signer is told a signature is being requested. **Exactly one method per signer** — the array shape is historical, and sending two returns `400`. The method must also be compatible with `verification_method`: `Email` verification takes `Email`, `Whatsapp` verification takes `Whatsapp`, and `DigitalCertificate` and `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` take either. WhatsApp incurs an additional cost and is available only on paid subscriptions. Omit it to have it inferred from `verification_method`, or `{"Email"}` when neither is sent. See **Verification & Notification Methods** for the full pairing table.

entries.description: Required for `collect`: field placements per page. In `collect`, every signer listed in `signers` must appear once and own at least one field here; otherwise `400`.

message.description: Text included in the invitation email.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601; default is no expiration. Must be at least one hour in the future. A UTC offset in the value is honored (`2026-12-31T23:59:59-03:00` is `2027-01-01T02:59:59Z`); a value without one is read as UTC, and a date alone (`2026-12-31`) means 23:59 UTC that day.

copy_receivers.description: Signer IDs that only receive a copy.

Envelope.description: Standard success wrapper. Operations add their own `data`.

status.description: HTTP status code, mirrored in the body.

Signer.description: A signing party belonging to a workspace account.

government_id.description: Signer's normalized CPF (11 digits) or CNPJ (14 characters; may be alphanumeric).

DisplaySettings.description: A field placement rectangle on a document page. Geometry values are pixels in Assinafy's 150-DPI page image, measured from the upper-left corner. Clients must keep the rectangle within the selected page's width and height; the API does not clamp out-of-bounds values.

left.description: Horizontal distance from the page's left edge, in page-image pixels.

top.description: Vertical distance from the page's top edge, in page-image pixels.

width.description: Width of the placement rectangle, in page-image pixels.

height.description: Height of the placement rectangle, in page-image pixels.

fontSize.description: Font size in the 150-DPI page-image coordinate system.

Document.description: A document and its current lifecycle state.

artifacts.description: Artifact download URLs keyed by name. Always `original`, plus `thumbnail` once one exists. A certificated document also carries `certificated`, `certificate-page` and `bundle`, and `pades` when it was signed with a digital certificate — the PAdES version holds the signers' ICP-Brasil signatures, which certification flattens out of the certificated PDF.

verification_code.description: The code printed on the certificate page. Anyone can check it with `GET /v1/documents/{verification_code}/verify` or on `verification_url`. `null` until the document is `certificated`, and on documents certificated before verification codes existed.

verification_url.description: The public verification page for this document. `null` until the document is `certificated`.

assignment.description: The document's assignment, or `null` before one is created. The server decides when it is included, whatever `expand` the request sends: the document list, `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}`, the signer's document list and document creation from a template always include it; `/documents/search` and the upload response never do. Only the rename response follows `?expand=assignment`.

pages.description: The document's pages. Included on the same responses as `assignment`, and also on the upload response.

has_contract.description: Only on `GET /v1/documents/{documentId}` read by the workspace, while the environment has contract tracking on: not with a signer's access code, not in document lists or webhooks, and left out when the lookup fails, so a missing key means unknown. Whether `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/documents/{documentId}/contract` answers with contract terms, the document's own or those of a contract it amends whose document still exists, so a page can lay out the contract section before reading it.

limits.description: Limits of the workspace's current plan. Returned only by `GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}`, not in account lists. More keys may be added.

webhook_endpoints.description: How many webhook endpoints the workspace can have: `1`, or `3` with the Multiple Webhooks feature. Creating one past the limit returns `403`.

DocumentContract.description: The contract terms tracked on a document.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code; `BRL` when a value is sent without one.

term.description: Steps on every renewal, starting at 1.

owner_id.description: ID of the workspace member who owns the contract. When the owner is no longer a member of the workspace (removed, left, or deleted with their account), the hourly run hands the contract to the first owner who is still an active member, or leaves it without one; an inactive member stays the owner. The contract's e-mails (renewal notice, expiring, expired, renewed) go to the first of the owner and the document's creator who is an active member, as that member's notification preferences allow.

metadata.description: Up to 50 keys of your own, each holding text of at most 500 characters; `null` when there are none. A key ending in `_at` cannot hold a number: the API returns numbers under such keys as dates.

external_references.description: IDs outside systems use for this contract, ordered by system and id.

document.description: Only with `expand=document`: the document the terms are tracked on.

amendments.description: Only on the single-contract read: the documents that amend, renew or terminate this contract, the applied ones first by `number`, then the pending ones.

DocumentContractInput.description: Every attribute is optional and only the ones sent change. `null` clears an attribute, except `auto_renew` (back to `false`) and `currency` (back to `BRL` while a `value` is set); `status` does not accept `null`. A changed `end_date` starts a new `term`.

status.description: On creation any status, so a contract that ended before it was tracked is registered as it ended: `expired` needs an `end_date` in the past, `terminated` its `end_date`; neither is walked by the lifecycle. Afterwards only `draft` or `active` (a contract in force never goes back to `draft`): `expired` and `terminated` are set by the lifecycle and the terminate endpoint; a closed contract is reopened by renewing it.

counterparty_name.description: Emoji are kept; other characters outside the 3-byte range are dropped.

counterparty_taxpayer_id.description: A valid CPF or CNPJ, formatted or not.

currency.description: Three letters, such as `BRL` or `USD`, stored in capitals; `BRL` when a `value` is set without one.

auto_renew.description: Whether the hourly run starts the next term the day after `end_date`, by `renewal_term_months`, instead of expiring the contract.

renewal_term_months.description: How far a renewal by the term moves `end_date`; 12 when unset.

notice_period_days.description: Days before `end_date` the notice period starts (`document_contract_renewal_notice`); none when unset.

owner_id.description: An active member of this workspace.

metadata.description: Your own fields: up to 50 keys of 1 to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, each holding plain text of at most 500 characters; no number under a key ending in `_at`, or `stuck_since`.

external_references.description: Replaces the whole list; `[]` or `null` clears it. Two items whose `system` and `id` compare equal case aside are one reference (the first sent is kept); a pair the database takes for one beyond that (accents, `ß` and `ss`) answers `400`.

system.description: Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`; stored in lower case.

id.description: Kept as sent; must not contain emoji or other 4-byte characters.

parent_document_id.description: Links the document as an amendment of this contract document, or of any document in its family (resolved to the root); `null` unlinks a pending amendment. With it, the other attributes are the terms the instrument changes, not terms of its own; on a pending amendment a `null` value drops that term from the delta rather than clearing it on the parent.

relation_type.description: Required on the first link. `amendment` may change `value`, `currency`, `start_date` (effective from, display only), `end_date`, `auto_renew`, `renewal_term_months`, `notice_period_days`, `counterparty_name`, `counterparty_taxpayer_id` and `metadata`; `renewal` only `end_date` and `value`; `termination` only `end_date` (the effective date).

updated_at.description: Optional precondition: the `updated_at` the client read the contract (or this document's amendment link) with, as the API returned it. If the contract or link changed since, nothing is written and the answer is `409` with `code: ContractChanged`. Not sent, or `null`: the write applies whatever changed meanwhile (last write wins). Compared to the second; a fraction of a second, as a JavaScript date prints it, is read and ignored. New terms and a first link have nothing to have read, so sending one answers `409`; on a pending amendment, send the link's own `updated_at` (the GET on that document).

DocumentContractAmendment.description: A document that amends, renews or terminates a contract: its link and the terms it changes. The parent's terms take the delta once this document is certificated; until then the parent is untouched.

document_name.example: Aditivo 1 - Contrato de prestação de serviços.pdf

parent_document_id.description: The contract document whose terms change.

number.description: Position among the parent's applied amendments by signing date; `null` while pending.

status.description: `applied` once the delta moved the parent's terms.

document_status.description: This document's own status, so a declined, cancelled or expired instrument shows as such. An instrument applies only while its document is `certificated`: one whose document reads `failed` after it was signed waits, with no `apply_error`, until it is certificated again, and then applies in its place in the signing order.

apply_error.description: Why a signed instrument has not applied yet, retried every hour: the workspace's plan does not include contract tracking (it applies on the first run after the plan returns), the parent would not take the delta, an instrument signed before this one has not applied yet, one signed after it has already applied (this one then stays blocked: unlink it, and record what it still changes on a new instrument), or an unexpected failure.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts in `terms` and `changes`. Once applied, the contract's currency at that moment, kept whatever the contract moves to later. While pending (and for an instrument applied before this was kept), the one this instrument moves the contract to, otherwise the contract's. `null` when neither has one.

terms.description: The delta: only the terms this instrument changes; `null` when it changes none (a termination on the day it is signed).

changes.description: Every parent field the roll-up moves, as `{from, to}`: a preview while pending, the record once applied; `null` when it moves none.

AssignmentSigner.description: A signer within an assignment: the base Signer plus per-assignment verification/notification details.

identity_verification_status.description: Latest identity-document verification status; `InReview` means the account must decide it before the document can be certificated.

notification_history.description: Per-channel delivery history for this signer (email + WhatsApp), most-recent send order.

NotificationHistoryEntry.description: A single notification delivery record for a signer channel.

field.description: Field definition associated with the item.

display_settings.description: Rendering metadata for the item. Collect items use the DisplaySettings schema; virtual and legacy items may return an empty or non-object value.

value.description: Captured value when completed; `null` until then.

Assignment.description: A request for signers to sign a document.

document_id.description: The document this assignment belongs to. `null` only if the document was deleted.

sender_email.description: Email of the user who sent the document; null once that user has deleted their account.

CostEstimate.description: Cost breakdown for an assignment plus current account balances. `credits` is the sum of `breakdown` (notifications, digital-certificate signatures and identity checks). `total_credits` is what the send will take from the credit balance: `credits`, plus `extra_document_cost` when `needs_extra_document` is true. The extra document is not a `breakdown` line.

credits.description: Sum of the `breakdown` costs: notifications, digital-certificate signatures and identity checks. Does not include the extra document.

needs_extra_document.description: True when the plan's document allowance is exhausted and an extra document will be charged from credits.

extra_document_cost.description: Credits for one extra document. Charged only when `needs_extra_document` is true.

total_credits.description: Credits the send will consume: `credits`, plus `extra_document_cost` when `needs_extra_document` is true.

The common ones: `user_name` (`assignment_created`, `user_rejected_document`); `signer_full_name` (every `signer_*` event and `signature_requested`); `signer_email`, `signer_whatsapp_phone_number` and `notification_method` (`signature_requested`); `reviewer_name` (identity review decisions); `error_message` (`document_processing_failed`). `message` already carries the actor's name, translated, so clients can show it as is. A `*_at` key inside the payload is returned as an ISO 8601 string here, as in every API response, but as a Unix integer in webhook bodies.

OAuthTokenRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/oauth/token`. Sent form-encoded per RFC 6749, or as JSON.

grant_type.description: `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` is for internal service clients only (Assinafy's own MCP server) — an ordinary confidential or public client authenticates with it and always gets `invalid_client`, exactly as an unrecognized client would. Everyday integrators use `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`.

code_verifier.description: RFC 7636: 43-128 characters from [A-Za-z0-9-._~]. Shorter values are rejected with `invalid_grant`.

client_secret.description: Confidential clients only. Public clients authenticate with PKCE and are never issued a secret; the token-exchange grant requires a confidential, internal-service client and therefore always requires this.

resource.description: RFC 8707 resource indicator. For `authorization_code`/`refresh_token`, optional; when present it must be the `resource` value published by /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and must match the one sent to /authorize, otherwise `invalid_target`. For the token-exchange grant it is REQUIRED and must equal this API's own resource identifier exactly (never a front-end resource such as the MCP server), otherwise `invalid_target`.

subject_token.description: Token-exchange grant only. The front-end resource's access token being traded in. Must be a live, original (never itself exchanged) token minted for a resource this server issues tokens for, other than this API's own audience.

subject_token_type.description: Token-exchange grant only. Required; only `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token` is supported.

requested_token_type.description: Token-exchange grant only. Optional; when present it must agree with the only type this server issues.

verification_method.description: Verification method. If provided without notification_methods, the notification method is inferred. Defaults to Email. Verification is never billed on its own — the cost comes from the notification it is paired with, so `Whatsapp` verification requires the WhatsApp notification and costs 0.45 credits per signer. `DigitalCertificate` adds the per-signer signature cost (0.5 credits) on top of the notification cost, and returns `400` when the template has placed signer fields. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires its account feature, requires the signer to have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee.

notification_methods.description: Notification method for this signer — exactly one, and it must be compatible with `verification_method`. If provided without verification_method, the verification method is inferred. Defaults to Email.

apiKeyAuth.description: Permanent API key (recommended for back-end integrations).
apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key

signerAccessCode.description: Signer access code used by signer-facing (Signing) endpoints instead of a user token: the code in the signer's signing link, sent as the `signer-access-code` query or body parameter. It can be used again and has no expiry; it stops working when the signing request is removed. Treat it as a secret.
signerAccessCode.name: signer-access-code

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with mandatory PKCE (S256), for applications and AI assistants acting in a user's workspace with that user's permission — as opposed to `apiKeyAuth`/`bearerAuth`, which authenticate the workspace or user directly. A token carries only the scopes the user approved and works for one workspace. Endpoints are published by the authorization server at `https://auth.assinafy.com.br/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. An OAuth token cannot reach billing, account lifecycle, credential management or admin surfaces regardless of scope. A missing scope answers `403` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"` naming it. See **OAuth Integration Guide** for the full flow.

scopes.documents:read: Read documents, their pages, tags, signers, assignments and activity, and the WhatsApp notifications sent for an assignment.
scopes.documents:write: Create, update and delete documents, and manage their signers, assignments and activity.
scopes.templates:read: Read reusable document templates, their pages, roles, fields and tags.
scopes.templates:write: Create, update and delete templates, their pages, roles, fields and tags.
scopes.account:read: Read the workspace's profile, theme and logo.
scopes.webhooks:write: Change the workspace's webhook subscription (delivery URL, events, contact email), deactivate it, manage webhook endpoints and re-send a delivery.
scopes.openid: Identify the authenticated user (OpenID Connect `sub` claim) and enable the `/v1/oauth/userinfo` endpoint.
scopes.profile: Include the user's name in the `id_token`/userinfo claims.
scopes.email: Include the user's email and its verification status in the `id_token`/userinfo claims.
scopes.offline_access: Request a refresh token, so the app keeps working after the user's session expires without prompting them again. Only granted to a client that explicitly asks for it.
